name: modbench
description: Modbench: install and order mods; view, edit, and compare Bethesda plugin files (.esp/.esm/.esl)

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Modbench is off until you trust this folder. It changes your mod files and runs git here.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Modbench
walkthroughs.description: From your mod manager's instance to your first edited plugin.

steps.title: Open your mod manager's instance
steps.description:
Open the folder where your mod manager keeps this instance. If VS Code opens it in Restricted Mode, Modbench is off until you trust it from the banner or from Modbench's views.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

steps.title: Your mods, plugins and downloads
steps.description:
The Mods, Plugins and Downloads views show your instance as your mod manager does: mod order, plugin order and the downloads folder. A change on disk shows up with no refresh.
[Show the Mods view](command:modbench.modList.focus)

steps.title: Put your modlist in git
steps.description:
Git Init Modlist makes the instance a repository, so each mod you edit gets source and history.
[Git Init Modlist](command:modbench.modlist.gitInit)

steps.title: Decompile a mod
steps.description:
Decompile and Commit Mod turns each plugin of a mod into plugin source: one JSON file for each record, in a repository of its own in source/. Right-click a mod that holds a plugin and has no source.
[Show the Mods view](command:modbench.modList.focus)

steps.title: Open a record
steps.description: Expand a plugin in the Plugins view and open a record. Edit a field in the record panel, or edit its plugin source file as text.

steps.title: Review the change
steps.description:
Each edit is a working-tree change. Diff it, discard it or commit it in Source Control.
[Open Source Control](command:workbench.view.scm)

steps.title: Build the plugin
steps.description:
Build Mod writes each plugin from its plugin source. The game, your mod manager and xEdit load the plugin.
[Build Mod](command:modbench.mod.build)

steps.title: Connect your agent
steps.description:
Modbench serves an MCP server, so an agent in VS Code reads your instance, runs its gestures and writes scripts.
[List MCP Servers](command:workbench.mcp.listServer)
[Set up your agent](https://github.com/WhiskyTangoFawks/ModBench/blob/main/docs/wiki/agent.md)

mods.description: The mods to build. Leave out to build every source mod.

modbench.attachToBackendPort.description: Attach to an mEdit already running on this port instead of starting one. Never a fallback: if nothing answers, Modbench reports it. Leave unset: each window starts its own mEdit.

modbench.stringsLanguage.description: The language a translated text shows in. A plugin's source keeps every language its strings hold.

modbench.agent.port.description: The port Modbench serves your agent's MCP server on, at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp. Set another for a workspace so two windows each have their own.

modbench.deployment.folder.description: The folder Deploy writes the active profile's load order into, as hardlinks. Set it for each instance, on the same volume as the instance.

modbench.mods.gameFolder.description: The game folder (the folder containing the game executable and Data/). A Steam install or a stock game folder. Leave blank to fall back to the mod manager's game path, then Steam auto-detect.

enumDescriptions: The day the copy was last modified.
A letter for the contents of the copy: A is the master's, so two cells with the same letter hold the same file.
modbench.mods.conflictTable.cellValue.description: What each cell of a mod's conflict table shows of its copy.

modbench.mods.greyInactiveFiles.description: Grey a file the game does not get, in the Mods view and the Explorer: another copy wins its path, it is excluded, or its mod is disabled.

modbench.mods.indicators.overwritesLoose.description: Overwrites loose files: badge a mod's row in the Mods view when a file of the mod wins over another copy.
Overwrites loose files: colour a mod's name in the Mods view when a file of the mod wins over another copy.

modbench.mods.indicators.overwrittenLoos.description: Overwritten loose files: badge a mod's row in the Mods view when a file of the mod loses to another copy, and the mod is not Redundant.
Overwritten loose files: colour a mod's name in the Mods view when a file of the mod loses to another copy, and the mod is not Redundant.

modbench.mods.indicators.redundant.badge.description: Redundant: badge a mod's row in the Mods view when the mod has a file the game could get, and every such file loses to another copy.

modbench.mods.indicators.redundant.colou.description: Redundant: colour a mod's name in the Mods view when the mod has a file the game could get, and every such file loses to another copy.

modbench.mods.indicators.containsExclude.description: Contains excluded files: badge a mod's row in the Mods view when the mod has an excluded file.
Contains excluded files: colour a mod's name in the Mods view when the mod has an excluded file.

modbench.mods.indicators.updateAvailable.description: Update available: badge a mod's row in the Mods view when the mod's version is older than the newest version check for updates found.
Update available: colour a mod's name in the Mods view when the mod's version is older than the newest version check for updates found.

modbench.mods.indicators.publisherTag.ba.description: Publisher tag: badge a row in the Mods view, and a file in the Explorer, with each publisher tag that covers it.

modbench.mods.indicators.publisherTag.co.description: Publisher tag: colour a mod's name in the Mods view when a publisher tag covers the mod.
